questions.q: What is a remediation workflow, as described in this lesson?
options: A repeatable process that turns root cause analysis and cleansing skills into something an organization can run consistently, without one-off ad hoc fixes
A single SQL script that fixes all data quality issues automatically
A dashboard that only displays issues without tracking them
A synonym for data profiling
questions.explain: Without a workflow, remediation becomes ad hoc, untracked, and issues quietly resurface.

questions.q: Put these remediation workflow stages in the correct order.
options: Detect, triage, assign, fix, verify
Verify, fix, detect, assign, triage
Assign, detect, verify, triage, fix
Fix, detect, triage, verify, assign
questions.explain: The lesson's five stages, in order, are detect, triage, assign, fix, then verify.

questions.q: Why is skipping the "verify" stage especially costly?
options: An issue marked 'fixed' but never re-checked creates false confidence in dashboards and reports
Verification is only a formality with no real consequence
It only affects automated remediation, never manual
SQL doesn't allow re-running a check twice
questions.explain: Verify re-runs the original check to confirm the violation is actually gone, not just assumed fixed.

questions.q: What is the tradeoff between automated and manual remediation described in this lesson?
options: Automated remediation scales to high-volume, well-understood patterns but a bad rule can mass-corrupt data fast; manual remediation handles ambiguous or risky cases but doesn't scale
Automated remediation is always safer than manual remediation
Manual remediation is only used for formatting dates
There is no meaningful difference between the two
questions.explain: A workflow often uses both — automated for the well-understood majority, manual for anything ambiguous.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend fixing data quality issues at the source system when possible?
options: A source fix means the data arrives correct everywhere the first time, instead of re-applying a warehouse-level patch on every single load forever
Source systems are always easier to access than a warehouse
Warehouse-level fixes are illegal under most data governance policies
Fixing at the source eliminates the need for a verify stage
questions.explain: Warehouse-only fixes don't propagate to other downstream copies and must be re-applied on every load.
